- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or overshoot after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 71.56→73.00, 71.98→75.19).
- Model underestimates late-period trends (last 5–10 days of 30d) — true values often rise faster than forecasted.
- Mean reversion is not captured: model fails to adjust downward after prolonged high prices, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Forecast lag: model reacts slowly to recent price drops or volatility, often missing short-term reversals.
- Overshoot correction: if forecast exceeds true value by >5% in consecutive days, reduce next-day forecast by 1–2% to align with observed mean reversion.
- Horizon bias: 30d forecasts are overly optimistic; consider weighting recent 10–15d data more heavily for short-term accuracy.
